schemas.notation: All listed fields required, only explicitly optional fields may be absent. Unions exact by kind/op. Strings own primitive data; uN is safe integer in stated range. Ref is an opaque registry-issued object, additionally session/provenance checked, not a forgeable label. Records have no symbol/extra/inherited enumerable fields; own accessors and array holes/extras reject without getter invocation. Cross-realm prototype identity is not checked. No undefined except named alternatives; unknown reason is host-only and presence is mandatory.
schemas.Limits: Exact numeric own keys in caps; omitted argument uses entire table; present record contains every key with finite nonnegative safe integer <= default (positive structural capacities). No unknown/undefined values, no per-call mutation; separately named reduced-limit cases are explicit.

Entry.label: <eval>|<print>|-|canonical absolute .cjs path; must correspond to kind
Entry.sourceSha256: 64 lowercase hex of UTF8 normalized source
Entry.rawSha256: 64 lowercase hex of selected original UTF8 bytes
Entry.base: fixed canonical virtual entry directory or invocation cwd

InvocationState.argv: dense string array <=argvEntries; exact CLI layout
InvocationState.env: own string data record <=envEntries; keys nonempty, no NUL or =

HostRequest.specifier: explicit ./ or ../ or absolute .json bounded string

schemas.TargetRef: Host opaque canonical target bound to actual namespace, session, invocation base, json purpose and authority; does not grant a stale lease or permit path/symlink races. readJson reauthorizes actual resource or refuses. Never exposed to guest.
schemas.sourceAcquisition: Command-owned sourceFile(path) or sourceStdin(), not provider channel requests; Entry receives already admitted source. Both share input/operation ledgers and cleanup. Provider cannot request sourceRead as a data bypass.

schemas.validationOrder: Validate enclosing schema first, then issued-reference/session provenance; use that first failing exact schema name in protocol diagnostic. HostRequest path descriptor before value; never invoke getters or coercion.

sessionMethods.drainToQuiescence: ():Promise<Quiescence|GuestErrorOutcome|ControlOutcome>; actual evaluator/job ownership, not poll-until-idle; once after provisional complete
sessionMethods.stop: (control:{origin:caller|execution|local|destination,reason:unknown}):void; closes guest scheduling/admission, idempotent; provider distinguishes destination retirement from caller cancellation of owned work
sessionMethods.close: ():Promise<void>; same idempotent completion, closes admission, drains registered cooperative resources and invalidates issued refs/channels

scopeMethods.registerCleanup: (cleanup:()=>void|Promise<void>):void; synchronous before acquisition, late registration refuses
scopeMethods.track: <T>(acquire:()=>T|Promise<T>,release:(value:T)=>void|Promise<void>):Promise<T>; registers before invoking acquire; retains/reaps admitted failures and late completions
scopeMethods.signal: borrowed actual invocation AbortSignal, not guest-accessible
scopeMethods.reserve: (resource:exactCapKey,units:nonnegativeSafeInteger):ReservationRef; before allocation/admission; commit/release witnessed, never reset cumulative ledger

providerContract.channel: Single invocation-bound request(req:HostRequest):Promise<HostReply>, never exposed to guest. Same-instance intrinsic adapts sync versus guest-Promise behavior. Caller cannot choose session/from/namespace through request fields.
providerContract.hostOwner: Command owns explicit grants, namespace/source admission, scope signal/control provenance, stdin, per-destination output owners, host-operation quotas and finally barrier; context.registerCleanup is used if present, but raw/custom context omission never removes owned finally cleanup.
providerContract.providerOwner: Provider owns evaluator/factory/guest cache/values/closures/errors/jobs, preallocation instrumentation and nonreentrancy. It must supply retirement evidence for close/create failures as well as normal completion.
providerContract.nonreentrancy: One executing guest turn per session. Control/host completion may update host records without reentering guest. Later reactions queue; no guest callbacks run while sync intrinsic is suspended. Cross-invocation execution allowed only with disjoint state.
providerContract.stopFailure: Raw escaping stop/close exceptions recorded with explicit presence. Earlier selected execution failure including undefined is retained; later cleanup cannot mask it. Continue registered retirement despite ordinary cleanup failure.

limitDefinitions.configuration: Only explicit case reductions from full defaults permitted by this candidate; all keys immutable after invocation starts. Default Limits hash is the canonical sorted-key JSON encoding of caps; future runner must bind it, no live limit changes.
limitDefinitions.containerEntries: Applies to each guest-created data record/array, argv/env/JSON records; fixed intrinsic seed and internal lexical environments are separately accounted, not reduced-limit user containers.
limitDefinitions.parserNesting: Maximum simultaneous source delimiter nesting AND parser/AST structural recursion depth128; enforce incrementally before descent, not after unbounded parse. EOF/comments/whitespace are not parserTokens; semicolon is one token.
limitDefinitions.readAggregate: Inline source bytes, source file/stdin, ordinary text and JSON content all count once per acquisition. Source stdin is not counted again as data. Cache hits do not reread content, but resolution requests and metadata work still count.
limitDefinitions.hostCalls: Actual content/metadata/stream-acquisition and sink operations, including adapter subcalls, not source-only estimates; stream chunks separately byte/work-accounted, never converted into Shell commands.
limitDefinitions.boundaries: All per-byte caps use bytes, all guestString/contextMember units UTF16 code units; KiB=1024, MiB=1048576. Failed-limit increments refuse before exceeding admitted capacity.
limitDefinitions.lowerLimits: Reserved seed65536 bytes/128 nodes and source/context requirements still apply. A reduction smaller than mandatory seed refuses as a retainedGuestBytes/guestNodes limit before guest effects, not an automatic pass.
